parts.text: A student investigates the cooling of hot water in a beaker. She uses the apparatus shown in Fig. 2.1. Fig. 2.1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Record room temperature θ R shown on the thermometer in Fig. 2.1. θ R = ......................................................... [1]

ms.label: 2(b)
ms.text:
read scale perpendicularly / or words to that effect
(e.g. at eye level, at right angles)

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Estimate what the temperature θ 300 is at 300 s. Use the readings from Table 2.1 to guide you. θ 300 = .....................................................°C [1]

parts.label: i
parts.text: (d) (i) Calculate the average cooling rate x 1 during the first 90 s of the experiment. Use the readings from Table 2.1 and the equation: x 1 = θ 0 – θ 90 T where T = 90 s and θ 0 and θ 90 are the temperatures at t = 0 and t = 90 s. Include the unit for the cooling rate. x 1 = ......................................................... [1]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Calculate the average cooling rate x 2 during the middle 90 s of the experiment. Use the readings from Table 2.1 and the equation: x 2 = θ 90 – θ 180 T where T = 90 s and θ 90 and θ 180 are the temperatures at t = 90 s and t = 180 s. x 2 = ......................................................... [1]

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Calculate the average cooling rate x 3 during the last 90 s of the experiment. Use the readings from Table 2.1 and the equation: x 3 = θ 180 – θ 270 T where T = 90 s and θ 180 and θ 270 are the temperatures at t = 180 s and t = 270 s. x 3 = ......................................................... [1]

ms.label: 2(e)(i)
ms.text:
description matching results
e.g. ‘cooling rate falls steadily as time goes on’ AND reference to cooling rate values to show this

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Estimate the final temperature θ F of the water after several hours. θ F = ......................................................... [1]

ms.label: 2(e)(ii)
ms.text: θ F near or equal to θ R

ms.label: 2(f)(i)
ms.text:
cooling rates likely to be lower
(e.g.) x2 lower than x1 and second 90 s has lower starting temperature

ms.label: 2(f)(ii)
ms.text:
any one suitable control variable from:
•
volume of water
•
size / material of beaker
•
room temperature / other valid environmental factor
